allow_large: The owner asked on 2026-09-29 for every review to run on Sol high; only forge.toml, init.py and review.py change behaviour, the other files are old tests that asserted xhigh
done_when: Every Forge review runs on GPT-6 Sol at high effort: this repo's forge.toml, the default forge init writes, and the prototype sign-off review's pinned model and effort; the light prototype review stays at medium; docs and skill text that name xhigh for reviews say high; tests check the default and the sign-off pin

findings.body: The branch adds only this tracking record. This repo's `forge.toml:40` and the default written by `src/forge/init.py:95` still set review effort to `xhigh`. Prototype sign-off is also pinned to `xhigh` at `src/forge/review.py:413`, and lines 384–385 reject a review reporting `high`. The requested cost fix therefore has no effect. The light prototype review remains at `medium` (`src/forge/review.py:368`).
findings.title: Not done: Every Forge review runs on GPT-6 Sol at high effort

findings.body: `tests/test_fix_autoreview_and_other_astra_passes_burn_t.py:9-13` exercises `forge init` but asserts that the generated review setting is `xhigh`. It would pass with the current, unwanted default. The branch needs this entry-point test to require GPT-6 Sol at `high`.
findings.title: Not done: forge init default test requires high effort

findings.body: `tests/test_proto_signoff.py:218-219` asserts that the sign-off command passes `codex=xhigh`, while lines 163–168 expect a review reporting `high` to be rejected. These entry-point checks enforce the opposite of the required pin and acceptance behavior, so they cannot catch this defect.
findings.title: Not done: prototype sign-off pin test requires high effort

why: Reviews run on GPT-6 Sol at xhigh effort, which costs more than the owner wants
